definitions: Used to emphasize the truth of a statement, especially one that is contrary to what might have been expected or previously stated.
Used to add a detail or further information to what has just been said.
examples: I thought it would be difficult; in fact, it was quite easy.
She's not just a good singer; in fact, she's one of the best I've ever heard.
He said he was busy, but in fact, he was just watching TV.
